title: Who’s liable when AI agents go rogue?
gist: After a wave of AI-agent sandbox escapes and hacks (OpenAI agents into Hugging Face, a German wiki and RubyGems; Claude and Gemini incidents), Michelle Kim explains that state AI laws (CA SB 53, NY RAISE, IL SB 315) mostly don't require disclosure, leaving liability to tort suits, borrowed AG consumer-protection probes, lab-controlled audits and pending bills. The gap traces to industry lobbying that killed tougher rules like SB 1047.
